Title: An Introduction to Hinduism
Creator: Gavin Flood
Notes: The standard academic introduction; strong on tantra, ritual and south Indian traditions. Flood already in People.

Title: Hinduism: A Very Short Introduction
Creator: Kim Knott
Notes: Pocket-sized expert overview (2nd ed.) including social media, popular culture and Hindu nationalism — ideal first read for students.

Title: The Infinite Stories of Hinduism (Crash Course Religions #5)
Creator: Crash Course
Notes: Part of the Pew-funded 2024 world religions series, also on PBS — polished classroom starter.

Title: Hinduism I: Sources and Development (lecture series)
Creator: Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies
Key Themes: Vedas, Upanishads, Gita, formation of traditions
Notes: OCHS's own free recorded lecture series — historical/thematic introduction from the Indus Valley onward.

Title: Hinduism Today (magazine)
Creator: Hinduism Today
Key Themes: contemporary Hinduism, practice, global Hindu life
Notes: Free quarterly from Kauai's Hindu Monastery (Saiva Siddhanta) — articulate insider journalism; single-tradition editorial stance.

Title: Introduction to Hinduism (Pluralism Project)
Creator: The Pluralism Project
Notes: Harvard project founded by Diana Eck; frames Hinduism through its American diaspora presence.

Title: Beliefs made visible: Hindu art in South Asia
Creator: Smarthistory
Notes: Free art-history introduction with quality images — good visual entry point.

Title: Hindu worldview traditions (subject knowledge essay)
Creator: RE:ONLINE
Notes: Expert essay by Catherine Robinson and Denise Cush written for UK RE teachers — includes guidance on representation and decolonising teaching.

Title: Hindu Myths: A Sourcebook Translated from the Sanskrit
Creator: Wendy Doniger
Notes: Seventy-five core myths translated from Sanskrit sources — the standard mythology sourcebook.

Title: Classical Hindu Mythology: A Reader in the Sanskrit Purāṇas
Creator: Cornelia Dimmitt, J.A.B. van Buitenen
Notes: Purāṇic myths organised by theme (Origins; Viṣṇu; Śiva; the Goddess); archive.org lending copy linked.

Title: Myth = Mithya: Decoding Hindu Mythology
Creator: Devdutt Pattanaik
Notes: Accessible handbook reading myths as cultural frames; popular not scholarly — pairs well with Doniger.

Title: Hindu Ideas of Creation (In Our Time: Religion)
Creator: BBC Radio 4
Notes: Melvyn Bragg with Jessica Frazier (OCHS), Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad and Gavin Flood; also on BBC Sounds.

Title: Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists
Creator: Sister Nivedita, Ananda K. Coomaraswamy
Notes: Free public-domain classic retellings with famous illustrations; colonial-era framing — read critically.

Title: The Difficulty of Being Good: On the Subtle Art of Dharma
Creator: Gurcharan Das
Notes: Mahābhārata ethics applied to modern life by a thoughtful non-academic — very teachable chapters per character.

Title: Hindu Ethics: A Philosophical Study
Creator: Roy W. Perrett
Notes: Concise analytic-philosophy treatment of classical Hindu ethics; archive.org lending copy linked.

Title: Hindu Philosophy (Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
Creator: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
Notes: Free peer-reviewed encyclopedia entry covering dharma and the puruṣārthas — citable and rigorous.

Title: An Autobiography: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
Creator: M.K. Gandhi
Notes: Primary source for ahiṃsā and satya in lived practice; free on archive.org.

Title: The Bhagavad Gita (In Our Time)
Creator: BBC Radio 4
Key Themes: Gita, dharma, duty, Krishna and Arjuna
Notes: With Jessica Frazier (OCHS), Julius Lipner and Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad — the dharma/duty dilemma, ideal A-Level listening; also on BBC Sounds.

Title: Addresses at the Parliament of Religions, Chicago 1893
Creator: Swami Vivekananda
Key Themes: Vivekananda, universalism, Hinduism in the West
Notes: Full text from Belur Math (Ramakrishna Mission) — the founding document of modern global Hinduism; public domain.

Title: The Hindu Diaspora: Comparative Patterns
Creator: Steven Vertovec
Notes: Includes a chapter directly on Britain's Hindu communities — core for the UK diaspora angle.

Title: Hindu Nationalism: A Reader
Creator: Christophe Jaffrelot
Notes: Primary-source excerpts from Hindutva thinkers with scholarly framing; politically sensitive — teach with care and balance.

Title: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London (Neasden Temple)
Creator: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir London
Notes: Britain's landmark mandir; site includes visitor and education information — obvious school-visit pairing.

Title: Religion in India: Tolerance and Segregation
Creator: Pew Research Center
Notes: 30,000-respondent survey of Indian religious life — free rigorous data for essays and statistics work.

Title: The Penguin History of Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300
Creator: Romila Thapar
Notes: The leading historian of early India; her secular historiography is contested by Hindutva critics — know both sides.

Title: The Wonder That Was India
Creator: A.L. Basham
Notes: Beloved classic survey, free on archive.org; scholarship now dated in places — use alongside Thapar.

Title: Harappa.com — The Ancient Indus Civilization
Creator: Harappa.com
Notes: Scholar-written essays and slideshows on the Indus civilisation, online since 1995 — feeds the origins controversy debate.

Title: The Camphor Flame: Popular Hinduism and Society in India
Creator: C.J. Fuller
Notes: The standard anthropological study of lived popular Hinduism — temples, possession, festivals, priests.

Title: Darśan: Seeing the Divine Image in India
Creator: Diana Eck
Notes: Short, teachable classic on seeing and being seen by the deity; Eck already in People.

Title: Diwali Objects Teacher Resource (Reading Museum)
Creator: Reading Museum
Notes: UK museum lesson pack with worksheets — pitched young; adapt upward for 16–18 or use for outreach.

Title: Hindu temples (Smarthistory)
Creator: Smarthistory
Notes: Free illustrated introduction to temple form and function.

Title: Speaking of Śiva
Creator: A.K. Ramanujan
Notes: Luminous translations of 12th-c. Kannada bhakti poets incl. Mahādēviyakka — bhakti as protest; full text on archive.org.

Title: A Storm of Songs: India and the Idea of the Bhakti Movement
Creator: John Stratton Hawley
Notes: Argues the unified 'bhakti movement' is a 20th-c. construction — sophisticated counterpoint for advanced students.

Title: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is (Vedabase)
Creator: A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada
Notes: Free searchable Gītā with Sanskrit, word-for-word gloss and devotional purports; interpretation reflects one tradition (ISKCON) — compare with academic translations.

Title: Hindu deities (Smarthistory)
Creator: Smarthistory
Notes: Clear free introduction to the major deities through art.

Title: Indian Philosophy: A Very Short Introduction
Creator: Sue Hamilton
Notes: Compact expert overview structured around the classical schools — right pitch for A-Level extension.

Title: A Source Book in Indian Philosophy
Creator: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, Charles A. Moore
Notes: 3,000 years of primary texts in one volume; Radhakrishnan's neo-Vedantin framing colours the selection — note when teaching.

Title: Classical Indian Philosophy (History of Philosophy Without Any Gaps)
Creator: Peter Adamson, Jonardon Ganeri
Notes: 60+ free episodes by two leading scholars — the best free deep resource on this strand; also an OUP book.

Title: Upaniṣads
Creator: Patrick Olivelle
Notes: The standard scholarly translation (Oxford World's Classics); Olivelle already in People.

Title: The Rigveda (3 vols)
Creator: Stephanie W. Jamison, Joel P. Brereton
Notes: First complete scholarly English translation in a century — the reference; Doniger's anthology (already in Hive) is the classroom entry.

Title: The Bhagavad Gita (Easwaran translation)
Creator: Eknath Easwaran
Notes: The most readable Gītā for students, with a 55-page contextual introduction; reverent insider translation, not text-critical.

Title: The Upanishads (In Our Time)
Creator: BBC Radio 4
Notes: With Jessica Frazier (OCHS), Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad and Simon Brodbeck; also on BBC Sounds.

Title: Annihilation of Caste
Creator: B.R. Ambedkar
Notes: Full text via Columbia — the essential primary source for the caste-critique side of this strand; Ambedkar already in People.
